label: MONEY LESSON
title: Profit is not cash
body: A business can show profit on paper and still run out of money. Profit is an accounting number. Cash is what pays salaries, rent and suppliers. Track both, every month.
caption: Many businesses that close were profitable on paper. They simply ran out of cash. Watch your cash flow as closely as your profit.

label: BUSINESS TERM
title: Break-even point
body:
The sales level where total revenue equals total cost. Below it you lose money, above it you earn.

Break-even units = Fixed costs ÷ (Price − Variable cost per unit)
caption: Before starting anything, know how much you must sell just to stop losing money. That number is your break-even point.

label: BUSINESS TERM
title: Gross profit vs Net profit
body:
Gross profit = Sales − Cost of goods sold.

Net profit = What is left after ALL expenses: rent, salaries, utilities, interest and tax.
caption: A high gross profit means nothing if your expenses eat all of it. Always look at net profit too.

label: BUSINESS TERM
title: Fixed vs Variable costs
body:
Fixed costs stay the same no matter how much you sell, like rent.

Variable costs rise and fall with sales, like raw material and packaging.
caption: Knowing which costs are fixed and which are variable is the first step to pricing your product correctly.

label: BUSINESS TERM
title: Working capital
body:
Working capital = Current assets − Current liabilities.

It shows whether a business can pay its short-term bills from its short-term resources.
caption: Negative working capital is an early warning sign. Healthy businesses keep enough to cover their near-term obligations.

label: MONEY LESSON
title: The power of compounding
body: Compounding means earning returns on your previous returns. Over time, growth builds on growth. The earlier you start, the more time does the heavy lifting.
caption: Time is the biggest ingredient in compounding. Small amounts started early can beat large amounts started late.

label: BUSINESS TERM
title: Opportunity cost
body:
The value of the next best option you give up when you make a choice.

Every decision has a hidden cost: what you could have done instead.
caption: When you choose one thing, you are also choosing not to do something else. Smart decisions count that cost too.

label: BUSINESS TERM
title: Contribution margin
body:
Contribution margin = Selling price − Variable cost per unit.

It is what each sale contributes toward covering fixed costs, and after that, toward profit.
caption: Products with a higher contribution margin do more work for your business. Know this number for everything you sell.

label: PRICING LESSON
title: Markup is not margin
body:
Cost 100, selling price 150.

Markup = 50 ÷ 100 = 50%
Margin = 50 ÷ 150 = 33.3%

Mixing them up leads to wrong pricing.
caption: Markup is calculated on cost. Margin is calculated on selling price. Same rupees, different percentages.

label: STARTUP TERM
title: Customer Acquisition Cost
body:
CAC = Total sales and marketing spend ÷ Number of new customers gained.

It tells you how much it costs to win one customer.
caption: If you do not know what it costs to get a customer, you cannot know if your growth is profitable.

label: STARTUP TERM
title: Customer Lifetime Value
body:
LTV is the total profit a customer brings over the whole relationship with your business.

If LTV is lower than the cost of acquiring that customer, growth burns money.
caption: Repeat customers are where real profit lives. Compare lifetime value with acquisition cost before spending on growth.

label: STARTUP TERM
title: Bootstrapping
body:
Building a business with your own savings and the revenue it earns, without outside investors.

You keep full ownership and control, but growth depends on your own cash.
caption: Many strong businesses started bootstrapped. It forces discipline: every rupee has to earn its place.

label: STARTUP TERM
title: MVP
body:
Minimum Viable Product: the simplest version of your product that lets you test whether people will actually use it and pay for it.

Launch small. Learn fast.
caption: Do not spend months perfecting something nobody has asked for. Build the simplest version and test it with real customers.

label: STARTUP TERM
title: Burn rate
body:
Burn rate is how much more cash a company spends than it earns, per month.

A company earning 2 lakh and spending 5 lakh has a burn rate of 3 lakh.
caption: Burn rate tells you how fast the money is disappearing. Every founder should know this number by heart.

label: STARTUP TERM
title: Runway
body:
Runway = Cash in bank ÷ Monthly burn rate.

30 lakh in the bank with a 3 lakh monthly burn means 10 months of runway.
caption: Runway is how many months you have before the money runs out. Plan your next move well before it ends.

label: BUSINESS TERM
title: Equity
body:
Equity is ownership in a company.

Giving away 20% equity means giving away 20% of the ownership and a 20% share in future profits.
caption: Equity is the most expensive thing a founder can give away. Understand it fully before you sign anything.

label: BUSINESS TERM
title: Revenue vs Net income
body:
Revenue is the total money earned from sales.

Net income is what remains after every expense is paid.

Big revenue does not always mean big earnings.
caption: Revenue is the top line. Net income is the bottom line. The bottom line is what you actually keep.

label: BUSINESS TERM
title: Depreciation
body:
Spreading the cost of a long-term asset, like a machine or vehicle, over its useful life instead of expensing it all at once.

It matches the cost with the years the asset is used.
caption: A machine that works for 10 years should not hit your profit all in one year. That is what depreciation fixes.

label: BUSINESS TERM
title: Inventory turnover
body:
How many times a business sells and replaces its stock in a period.

Slow turnover means money is sitting on shelves instead of working for you.
caption: Stock that does not move is cash that is stuck. Fast-moving inventory keeps a business healthy.

label: MONEY LESSON
title: Build an emergency fund
body:
A common guideline is to keep 3 to 6 months of essential expenses saved before you start investing or taking big risks.

It protects you when life surprises you.
caption: An emergency fund is not an investment. It is protection, so one bad month does not become a crisis.

label: MONEY LESSON
title: What inflation does
body:
When prices rise, the same amount of money buys less.

Money kept idle for years quietly loses its value.
caption: Inflation is a silent cost. Understanding it is the first step to protecting what you earn.

label: MONEY LESSON
title: Diversification
body:
Spreading your money across different investments so that one loss does not sink everything.

In simple words: do not put all your eggs in one basket.
caption: Diversification does not remove risk, but it stops a single bad outcome from wiping you out.

label: PRICING LESSON
title: Price on value, not just cost
body:
Cost tells you the minimum you can charge.

The value your customer sees tells you what you could charge.

The best pricing sits between the two.
caption: Cost-plus pricing is a floor, not a strategy. Understand what your product is worth to the customer.

label: BUSINESS TERM
title: Receivables
body:
Receivables are money your customers owe you for sales made on credit.

A credit sale is not cash until it is collected.
caption: Selling is half the job. Collecting is the other half. Keep a close eye on who owes you and for how long.

label: MONEY LESSON
title: The Rule of 72
body:
Divide 72 by the yearly return rate to estimate how many years it takes for money to double.

At 12% a year: 72 ÷ 12 = about 6 years.
caption: A quick mental shortcut every investor should know. It is an estimate, but a surprisingly good one.

label: BUSINESS TERM
title: Overheads
body:
Ongoing business costs that are not tied to one specific product: rent, utilities, admin salaries, internet.

They must be covered whether you sell or not.
caption: Overheads are easy to ignore and hard to cut later. Keep them lean, especially in the early days.

label: BUSINESS TERM
title: Economies of scale
body:
As production grows, the cost per unit usually falls, because fixed costs are spread over more units.

This is why big players can often sell cheaper.
caption: Scale changes the math of a business. More units can mean a lower cost for each one.

label: BUSINESS TERM
title: Liquidity
body:
How quickly an asset can be turned into cash without losing value.

Cash is the most liquid asset. Property and machinery are much less liquid.
caption: Owning valuable assets is not the same as having money available. Liquidity is what saves you in a tight spot.

label: BUSINESS TERM
title: Assets vs Liabilities
body:
Assets are what you own that has value: cash, stock, equipment, money owed to you.

Liabilities are what you owe: loans, unpaid bills, payables.
caption: Assets minus liabilities gives equity, the true value that belongs to the owner.

label: MONEY LESSON
title: Ignore sunk costs
body:
A sunk cost is money already spent that cannot be recovered.

Good decisions look at future costs and benefits only, not at what is already gone.
caption: "I have already spent so much on this" is not a reason to keep going. Decide based on what comes next.
